MOLECULAR CYTOGENETICS LABORATORY
FLUORESCENCE IN SITU HYBRIDIZATION (FISH) REPORT

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Medical Record Number: [redacted ID]
Date of Birth: [redacted]
Specimen ID: [redacted ID]

SPECIMEN DETAILS
Specimen Type: Lymph node biopsy
Date Collected: [redacted]
Date Received: [redacted]
Date Reported: [redacted]

CLINICAL INFORMATION
Clinical Diagnosis: Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma (DLBCL), non-germinal center type
Reason for Referral: FISH analysis for B-cell lymphoma panel

TEST PERFORMED
Interphase FISH Analysis - B-Cell Lymphoma Panel

METHODOLOGY
Interphase fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) was performed on formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tissue sections using the following probe sets:
• BCL6 (3q27) Break Apart Probe
• MYC (8q24) Break Apart Probe
• IGH/BCL2 Dual Color Dual Fusion Probe [t(14;18)]
• IGH/MYC/CEP8 Tri-Color Probe

A minimum of 200 interphase nuclei were analyzed for each probe set.

RESULTS

BCL6 (3q27) REARRANGEMENT STATUS: POSITIVE
• Rearrangement detected in 85% of nuclei analyzed (170/200)
• Normal signal pattern: 15% (30/200)
• Cutoff for positive result: >10%

MYC (8q24) REARRANGEMENT STATUS: NEGATIVE
• No rearrangement detected
• Copy number: 2-7 copies per nucleus (average 4.2)
• Amplification pattern observed in 65% of cells

IGH/BCL2 t(14;18) STATUS: NEGATIVE
• No IGH/BCL2 fusion signals detected
• BCL2 (18q21) copy number: 2-5 copies per nucleus (average 3.1)
• IGH (14q32) copy number: 1-2 copies per nucleus
• Loss of one IGH signal in 45% of cells analyzed

IGH/MYC FUSION STATUS: NEGATIVE
• No IGH/MYC fusion signals detected
• CEP8 control signals: 2-4 per nucleus

INTERPRETATION
This FISH analysis demonstrates:

1. BCL6 gene rearrangement at 3q27, which is consistent with the diagnosis of Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma (DLBCL) and is observed in approximately 30-40% of DLBCL cases.

2. Absence of MYC rearrangement and IGH/BCL2 fusion, ruling out double-hit lymphoma involving these loci.

3. Copy number alterations including:
   • Multiple copies of MYC (2-7 copies) without rearrangement
   • Multiple copies of BCL2 (2-5 copies) without IGH/BCL2 fusion
   • Loss of one IGH signal in a subset of cells

The clinical significance of the observed copy number variations (increased MYC and BCL2 copies with IGH loss) in the absence of gene rearrangements is unclear. These findings may represent chromosomal instability or aneuploidy commonly seen in aggressive B-cell lymphomas.

The BCL6 rearrangement is consistent with DLBCL and other B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphomas. BCL6 rearrangements can occur in both germinal center and non-germinal center subtypes of DLBCL.
